definitions.explanation: The vertical distance from the surface of a body of water to its bottom. Used in geography, navigation, diving, and pool measurements.

examples.japanese: このプールの{水深|すいしん}は1.2メートルだ。
examples.english: The depth of this pool is 1.2 meters.

examples.japanese: {水深|すいしん}200メートルを{超|こ}えると、{太陽|たいよう}の{光|ひかり}はほとんど{届|とど}かなくなる。
examples.english: Beyond a depth of 200 meters, sunlight barely reaches.

notes:
{水深|すいしん} refers to the depth of water — how deep a body of water is at a given point.

FORMS:
{水|すい} (water) + {深|しん} (depth). The same pattern appears in {海深|かいしん} (ocean depth).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {水深|すいしん}〜メートル: depth of ~ meters
- {水深|すいしん}が{深|ふか}い/{浅|あさ}い: deep/shallow water
- {最大|さいだい}{水深|すいしん}: maximum depth
- {水深|すいしん}を{測|はか}る: to measure water depth

USAGE:
Used in maritime navigation, scuba diving, fishing, and geographic descriptions. Often appears on nautical charts and diving information.

RELATED WORDS:
- {水位|すいい}: water level (height of water surface)
- {深海|しんかい}: deep sea
- {浅瀬|あさせ}: shallows, shoal
